name: PSA-fs
title: FS series high-capacitance multilayer ceramic chip capacitors, 1 µF and up
summary: The FS series is a family of class II surface-mount MLCCs of 1 µF and more, in sizes 0201 to 2225, with X7R, X7S, X6S, X5R and Y5V dielectrics and rated voltages from 4 V to 630 V. Inside, several capacitor sections are stacked in series so the voltage stress is spread across the body, a construction meant to prevent short-circuit failure. Terminations are lead-free with a pure tin finish; the parts are halogen-free, RoHS compliant and unpolarised.

operation.text: Each chip holds several multilayer capacitor sections connected in series, so the applied voltage is shared among them and the voltage gradient is spread through the whole body; the aim is to avoid short-circuit failure. It is designed as a safety part for LCD backlight inverters.
Coupling and decoupling in digital circuits, bypass, smoothing, and DC-DC converters. Suited to both wave and reflow soldering, within the size and capacitance limits of the soldering method tables.

Before capacitance and dissipation are checked the parts are heated to 150 °C for an hour and left 24 hours at room temperature; capacitance is then read at 1 kHz, 1 Vrms up to 10 µF and at 120 Hz, 0.5 Vrms above, at 25 °C (20 °C for Y5V).

In the high-temperature load test the voltage stays at 100 % of rated up to 100 °C for 125 °C parts, 80 °C for 105 °C parts and 60 °C for 85 °C parts, then falls linearly to 70 % at the part's maximum temperature.

Store indoors at 5 to 40 °C and 20 to 70 %RH, away from sulfuric acid, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and chlorine and out of direct sunlight; keep the pack sealed until use and re-seal it once opened. Use within 12 months of shipment, checking solderability first.
The ceramic is hard and brittle and chips or cracks under mechanical abuse. Pick parts up with vacuum or plastic tweezers; taped parts suit automatic placement.

Preheat at no more than 3 °C per second to limit thermal shock. Use mildly activated rosin fluxes (RA, RMA), never activated flux, and keep the solder volume controlled so the joint does not stress the chip. By hand: tip diameter 1.0 mm or less, 20 W max., melt the solder on the tip, keep the tip off the ceramic, and let the board cool in still air with no forced cooling.
The solder fillet should climb at least 25 % of the chip thickness or 500 µm, whichever is less (after IPC-610E).
Let the board and parts cool naturally in air after soldering. Remove all flux residue, including under the chips, with an electronics-grade solvent; ultrasonic cleaning works well.
